summary: Steel fire tower on Chopmist Hill in Scituate, RI, administered by RIDEM; NHLR-registered 2014, re-roofed by ham radio operators and former or current emergency personnel in 2022, cab locked and unstaffed per 2016 visit reports.

facts.design: Steel tower; the Register says a steel tower replaced an earlier wooden one in 1946 and that the current tower is the third on the site

access.note: Perimeter fence; cab access door locked; no NHLR sign or directions signed (2016 visit report). No current access rule found.

facts.agency: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management

events.note: State forestry report lists a 40-foot wood tower on Chopmist Hill.
Commissioner's report calls the tower in very bad condition and unfit for further use; recommends a steel replacement.
State report says a new 60-foot steel observation tower replaced the old wooden tower that year.
NHLR build year: a steel tower replaced the original wooden tower in approximately the same location as the current tower. Conflicts with the 1926 report.
Louise Ide retired June 30 as Chopmist Hill Tower Observer after 25 years.

Trees around the tower had grown so tall that fire wardens had trouble seeing past them; Calvin Dunwoody, chief of the Division of Forests, said trimming would cost too much because the trees were on private property.
Registered September 2, 2014 as US 1016, RI 5; nominated by Henry Isenberg.
Ham radio operators and former or current emergency personnel re-roofed the tower in Scituate.

corrections.why: 12.2 m (40 ft) matches the 1918 report of a 40-foot wood tower, not the current tower. The 1926 steel tower was 60 feet (18.3 m). No height for the current tower appears in the sources read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says a steel tower replaced the original wooden tower in 1946 and that the current tower is the third on the site. The Forest Lookouts quotes a 1926 state report describing a new 60-foot steel tower that replaced the old wooden tower that year. The sequence cannot be reconciled from these sources, so the story reports both dates.

notes_for_editor: Build date conflicts: NHLR gives 1946 for the current steel tower; a 1926 state report describes a steel tower erected that year. Height in the brief (12.2 m) matches the 1918 wooden tower and should not be used for the current tower. Staffing and access rest on 2015-2016 NHLR visit reports; the newest visit report is dated December 15, 2016, so present condition and access are unconfirmed. Elevation matches the brief (730 ft, 223 m; the brief's 222.5 m is consistent). No specific fire spotted by this tower was found in the sources read. The 2022 PDF is the Rhode Island chapter's annual report, so the state in its restoration line is Rhode Island (it also names Pine Hill in Exeter, RI).
